prerequisites: Organic Chemistry examination must be passed prior to Biochemistry

learning_outcomes.text: The Student will know structures and properties of the main classes of biological molecules such as proteins, carbohydrates and lipids, and moreover the main degradative pathways involved in the energetic metabolism.
The Student will be able to apply her/his previous knowledge in the fields of General, Organic and Physical Chemistry to a physiological context.
The Student will be able to integrate the acquired knowledge within a coherent frame.

syllabus_topics: Introduction: Main classes of biological molecules; energetic metabolism and ATP; recall about water molecule properties (hydrogen bonds, water interactions with polar, apolar and amphipathic solutes); recalls about acid-base equilibria and buffers.

Amino acids: classification and nomenclature of standard alpha-amino acids; acid-base properties and titration curves; peptide bond; polypeptide conformations; polypeptide ionization; protein structure levels; secondary structure elements, fibrous proteins: alpha-keratin, collagen, fibroin; globular proteins; proteins denaturation.

Myoglobin and Hemoglobin: oxygen transport; Hemoglobin cooperative binding; the Hill
M
and the Adair
M
models; the Bohr effect; modulation of Hemoglobin by CO2, H+ and 2,3-BPG; molecular basis of sickle-cell anemia.
Main enzymic mechanisms; vitamins, cofactors, coenzymes; enzymatic activity regulation and allosteric modulation; fundamentals of enzyme inhibition: competitive, uncompetitive and mixed inhibition.

Carbohydrates: classification and nomenclature of monosaccharides; cyclic hemiacetals and hemiketals formation; anomers and epimers; acetals and ketals formation; the glycosidic bond, disaccharides; polysaccharides: cellulose, amylose, amylopectin, glycogen.

Lipids: classification and nomenclature of fatty acids and lipids; triacylglycerols, glycerophospholipids, glycolipids, sphingolipids, and wax esters; sterols; physical properties and aggregation states; biological membranes.
Metabolism: general overview; ATP and phosphoryl-transfer; main redox coenzymes; Glycolysis; homolactic and alcoholic fermentation; Gluconeogenesis.

Pyruvate oxidative decarboxylation; Citric acid cycle; Respiratory chain; Oxidative phosphorylation; lipids digestion and absorption; beta-oxidation of fatty acids; amino acids transamination, oxidative deamination; Urea cycle.
assessment_rules: The examination is an individual colloquium, also requiring the use of graphics, equations, schemes, flux diagrams. The final decision considers meaningfulness, knowledge of scientific language and specific course contents, ability to correlate notions, ability to relate different frames, and ability to use graphics, equations, schemes, flux diagrams, chemical structural formulae. A grade of 18-30 is considered sufficient, while 1-17 indicates serious errors, and 0 means no answer was provided.
